hero.title: Global Security and Energy Markets Remain Under Pressure as Middle East and Ukraine Conflicts Escalate
hero.description: A new Houthi attack claim involving Riyadh, continued disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, a major drone attack on Moscow and fresh US-China economic talks are among the leading international stories this Sunday.
hero.imageQuery: global world news map Middle East energy shipping

breaking: 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh by Yemen's Houthi movement; no casualties were reported.
🚨 Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks against sensitive sites in Riyadh and an Aramco facility in Yanbu. The claims about specific damage remain subject to verification.
🛢️ Strait of Hormuz shipping remains severely disrupted. Preliminary data showed only four commodity vessels crossed on Thursday, compared with a 10-day average of about 16.
🚢 Three LNG vessels have reappeared outside the Strait of Hormuz, while some vessels continue using routes that are difficult to track.
🇷🇺 Russia says more than 1,600 drones were shot down since Saturday, including about 450 approaching Moscow. Two people were killed in the Moscow region and an oil refinery in Moscow was hit.
🇺🇸🇨🇳 US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are due to meet in New York for talks covering trade, tariffs, AI and critical minerals.
🇺🇳 Nearly 130 heads of state are expected in New York for the UN General Assembly, with the Middle East, Ukraine, energy security and AI governance among the major issues.
🇨🇦🇪🇺 Canada and the European Union are discussing a proposed closer partnership. Canada is not joining the EU, and the proposed 'associate member' status does not currently exist under EU treaties.
🇳🇬 Dangote Refinery's $1.6 billion IPO remains a major Nigerian business story, with 4.1 billion shares offered at ₦525 each.
🇹🇷🇸🇦 Turkey says it is prepared to provide military technical support to Saudi Arabia under its new defence arrangement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.
🌍 Global shipping costs remain elevated as energy disruption forces some vessels to take longer and more expensive routes.

featured.title: Hormuz Shipping Remains Severely Disrupted as Saudi Arabia Faces New Houthi Attacks
featured.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains one of the world's most closely watched shipping routes. Preliminary tracking data showed four commodity vessels crossing the waterway on Thursday, compared with a 10-day average of about 16. Some vessels may not appear in tracking data because their identification systems have been switched off. At the same time, several LNG vessels have reappeared outside the Strait. Saudi Arabia is also trying to maintain oil exports through alternative routes, including ship-to-ship transfers involving Oman's Sohar port.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Reports Missile Intercepted Over Riyadh
articles.content: Saudi Arabia says its air defences intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh by Yemen's Houthi movement. No casualties were reported. The Houthis also claimed to have attacked sensitive locations in Riyadh and an Aramco facility in Yanbu. Those specific claims have not been independently verified. The attacks come as fighting involving Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis expands along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
articles.imageQuery: Riyadh Saudi Arabia skyline missile defence

articles.title: Hormuz Traffic Remains Far Below Normal
articles.content: Preliminary Kpler shipping data recorded four commodity vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, compared with a 10-day average of about 16. The route previously carried a major share of global oil and gas shipments. Tracking data may undercount vessels using so-called dark routes with their transponders switched off. Three LNG vessels have also reappeared outside the Strait, suggesting some movement is gradually resuming.
articles.imageQuery: Strait of Hormuz commercial ships tanker

articles.title: US and China Prepare for Fresh Economic Talks
articles.content: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are scheduled to meet in New York for discussions on trade, tariffs, artificial intelligence and critical minerals. The talks come ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Several major trade and economic disagreements remain unresolved, including tariffs and China's supply of critical minerals.
articles.imageQuery: US China trade talks flags diplomacy

articles.title: Massive Drone Attack Reported Around Moscow
articles.content: Russian authorities say more than 1,600 drones have been intercepted since Saturday, including around 450 approaching Moscow. Two people were killed in the surrounding Moscow region and drones reached an oil refinery in the Russian capital. Smoke was seen rising from the facility, although the full extent of the damage remains unclear. Ukraine has not commented on the reported attack.
articles.imageQuery: Moscow Russia oil refinery smoke drone attack

articles.title: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery IPO Continues to Attract Strong Interest
articles.content: Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering remains one of Nigeria's biggest business stories. The company is offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each, targeting about ₦2.15 trillion, or roughly $1.6 billion. The refinery currently has capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and plans to expand towards 1.4 million barrels per day. Digital investment platforms experienced heavy traffic when the IPO opened, while regulators have warned investors about impersonation and phishing scams.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Uses Alternative Export Routes
articles.content: Saudi Arabia is working to maintain crude exports despite disruption to its East-West pipeline and attacks affecting regional infrastructure. Trade sources say Saudi Aramco plans to move significant volumes through ship-to-ship transfers near Oman's Sohar port during September and October. The additional supply is helping offset reduced shipments from Yanbu and has contributed to some downward pressure on oil prices.

articles.title: AI Governance Returns to the International Agenda
articles.content: Artificial intelligence is expected to feature prominently in international discussions this week. US-China officials are including AI in their economic talks, while the United Nations General Assembly is expected to examine questions surrounding international AI governance and safeguards. The debate centres on how governments can encourage technological development while managing security, economic and social risks.
articles.imageQuery: artificial intelligence global technology digital network

articles.title: Asia Watches Energy and Trade Developments Closely
articles.content: Asian economies remain closely exposed to developments in the Middle East because several major economies depend heavily on imported oil and gas. Saudi Arabia's alternative export routes are helping maintain supplies to Asian buyers, while shipping risks around Hormuz continue to raise transport and insurance costs. China, India, Japan and South Korea are among the major buyers affected by changes in regional energy flows.

morningSummary: Good morning. Global attention remains focused on the Middle East, where Saudi Arabia says it intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh while the Houthis claim further attacks on Saudi targets. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted, although some LNG movement is beginning to reappear. Russia is reporting one of its largest recent drone attacks around Moscow, while US and Chinese officials prepare talks on trade, tariffs, AI and critical minerals. Nearly 130 world leaders are expected at the United Nations this week. In Nigeria, the Dangote Refinery IPO continues to attract strong public interest as the company seeks to raise about $1.6 billion for expansion.
bigQuestion: With conflicts now affecting energy supplies, shipping, trade, technology and international relations, what should world leaders prioritise first: security, diplomacy or economic stability?
